correctness.rationale: Direct distance-table decomposition has strictly negative fluctuation sectors for 0<p<2 by the strict negative type of collinear real points. The symmetric radial sector is <0 by concavity for p<p_0<1. The antisymmetric 2x2 sector is equivalent to the stated determinant with X,Z>0. At p=0 determinant tends to 1; at p_0 X=0 and Y<0, hence a root. Li–Weston strict-inheritance excludes multiple singular exponents. The endpoint kernel is exactly one-dimensional. The t-boundary and q-asymptotic expansions are derived analytically. The included checker supplies exact rational identities plus finite full-matrix tests, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: An infinite natural graph-metric family has an exact negative-type threshold with a one-dimensional embedding-rank transition; more unusually, a pendant-edge perturbation lowers the exponent at every finite length yet recovers the core value at both endpoints, and the large-branching coefficient produces a provable noncommutation of limits. The quantitative singular limit is mathematically specific, natural, and not a trivial restatement of a generic distance-matrix algorithm.
